note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: You are writing an isolation procedure for a new bottling machine in a juice factory in St. Catherine. Where do you start?
options: Copy the procedure written for a different machine in the same plant
Survey the machine and its drawings for every energy source
Ask the operators which switch they usually turn off at night
Write down the steps the maker gives for starting the machine

questions.stem: Why does an isolation procedure name each isolation point by a unique label, such as 'MCC-3 Isolator 12'?
options: So that the isolator can be ordered again from the supplier
So the procedure matches the layout of the maker's manual
So operators know which isolator cost the most money
So nobody locks off the wrong isolator by mistake

questions.stem: A production line has a filler, a capper and a conveyor between them. Why is it shut down in the order the procedure gives?
options: To clear product safely and stop jams or spills
So that each machine uses less power as it slows down
So that all the isolators can be opened at the same instant
Because the maker charges less if the machines stop in order

questions.stem: Which device is a proper point of isolation for maintenance on a 220 V machine?
options: A start/stop push-button station mounted on the machine
A speed drive's 'safe stop' input wired to a key switch
A lockable isolator that opens all live conductors
A time switch that turns the machine off every night

questions.stem: Inside an isolated control panel, some wires are a different colour and labelled 'external supply'. What does this warn you of?
options: Those wires are spares and can be cut back safely
Those wires are earth conductors and carry no voltage
They may still be live from another source
They carry signals that are too small to matter

questions.stem: A pump at a water plant is fed by solar panels through a DC isolator and an inverter. In daylight, after the DC isolator is opened, which part is still live?
options: The cables between the panels and the DC isolator
The motor terminals on the far side of the inverter
The AC breaker in the main switchboard of the plant
The earth bar inside the inverter's enclosure

questions.stem: A machine's control panel is backed up by a UPS (uninterruptible power supply). What must the isolation plan include?
options: Nothing extra, as a UPS only works during a power cut
Unplugging the UPS from its wall socket and nothing more
Switching the UPS display off with its front button
Isolating the UPS output, as it can keep the circuit live

questions.stem: Why is an isolation plan checked against the latest drawings, not just an older printed procedure?
options: Old procedures are always written in too simple a way
The machine may have been changed or added to since
New drawings are much easier to read on a phone
The drawings show the price of each part to be isolated

questions.stem: A three-phase machine with a neutral is to be proved dead at its terminals. How many tests between pairs of conductors, earth included, are needed?
A 220 V single-phase machine in Jamaica is fed by L1, L2, neutral and earth. How many tests between pairs are needed to prove it dead fully?
Why should the voltage tester used to prove dead have shrouded probes with only a small metal tip showing?
options: So that it fits more easily into a tool bag
To lower the risk of a short circuit or flash at the terminals
So that the tester can read much higher voltages
So that the tester no longer needs to be checked

questions.stem: The leads of your approved voltage tester are found damaged on site. What should you do?
options: Tape over the damaged part and carry on testing
Borrow a multimeter and set it to resistance
Use a non-contact pen instead for the rest of the job
Stop and get an approved tester and leads

questions.stem: Eight workers from three trades will work on a large mixer at the same time. Which method keeps the isolation simple and safe?
options: One lock is fitted by the supervisor on behalf of everyone
Each worker writes their own name on the one tag
The isolator key is kept in the supervisor's office
Isolation keys go in a lockbox and each worker locks the box

questions.stem: What is an isolation certificate or permit to work used for?
options: To show that the machine was bought new and is under warranty
To record the isolations made and authorise the work
To allow work to begin while the isolation is still being done
To replace the need for each worker to fit a personal lock

questions.stem: At shift change, work on an isolated machine will continue with a new team. What is the safe practice?
options: The first team leaves its locks on and goes home as usual
The first team takes its locks off before the new team arrives
The new team fits its locks before the old team removes theirs
The supervisor holds all the lock keys until the morning

questions.stem: A worker has gone home with a personal lock still on an isolator. Under a typical procedure, who may authorise its removal?
options: A named manager, after checks that the worker is not at the machine
Any electrician on site who has a pair of bolt cutters
The machine operator, if production is waiting
The next person who needs to use the machine

questions.stem: A capacitor of 1 000 µF (0.001 F) is charged to 400 V. Using E = ½CV², how much energy does it hold?
A speed drive's label says 'Wait 5 minutes after removing power'. What should you do before touching its DC terminals?
options: Wait the stated time, then test that the DC bus is dead
Short the terminals with a screwdriver to save time
Wait one minute, because the label allows a margin
Touch the terminals lightly with the back of your hand

questions.stem: A hydraulic press has an accumulator. After the pump is isolated, what must be done?
options: Nothing more, because the pump makes all of the pressure
Loosen a hose fitting a little to see whether oil comes out
Run the pump briefly so that the accumulator empties
Release the pressure as the maker says; check the gauge is at zero

questions.stem: A conveyor has a heavy take-up weight that keeps the belt tight. What should be done before working on the belt?
options: Cut the belt so the weight drops down to the floor
Ask someone to hold the weight up by hand while you work
Lower or secure the weight as the procedure shows
Run the conveyor backwards for a moment to loosen it

questions.stem: A compressed-air line to a machine is isolated by a valve. Why should the valve be a lockable type with a way to vent trapped air?
options: So that the trapped air can be saved and used again later
So that the air is cooler by the time the work starts
So it can be locked shut and the trapped air let out
So that the compressor runs less often during the job

questions.stem: A steam line feeds a dryer. Why is a 'double block and bleed' arrangement used to isolate some lines?
options: It lets the line run safely at twice its normal pressure
It makes the line much easier to paint and keep clean
It speeds up the flow when the line is opened again
Two shut valves with a vent between them stop leaks

questions.stem: Before shutting down a cold store's compressor for repair, what should you plan with the owner?
options: How the stock will be kept cold
Which paint colour the new parts will be
How many staff will want to watch the work
What the compressor cost when it was new

questions.stem: An isolator is marked 'Do not operate under load'. What does this tell you?
options: It may only be opened while the machine is running
Stop the machine first; it is not made to break the current
It can be opened by anyone without a permit to work
It can be used as the machine's emergency stop

questions.stem: During the 'try' step, the machine starts. What must you do?
options: Stop it, keep everyone clear and find the missed supply
Let it run, since this proves the motor is in good order
Press start again to make sure it really did start
Carry on with the job, as the isolator is locked anyway

questions.stem: After the 'try' step, why must the start controls be returned to OFF?
options: So that the machine looks tidy for the client
So it cannot start the moment power is restored
So that the control circuit fuse does not blow
So that the operator's own tag can be taken off

questions.stem: A guard door interlock stops a machine when the door is opened. Why is this NOT enough for maintenance work inside the guard?
options: Interlocks do not work properly in hot weather
An interlock only stops the machine for a minute
It is a control device that can fail or be bypassed
Opening the door uses up all the stored energy

questions.stem: A PLC (programmable controller) screen shows a machine as 'stopped'. What does this tell you about isolation?
options: The machine is isolated and it is safe to work on
All of the machine's stored energy has been released
The power to the motor has been fully removed
Nothing; a control signal is not an isolation

questions.stem: As isolation supervisor, how do you check that a team member's lock is on the right isolator?
options: Ask them if they are sure, and then carry on
Count the locks left in the store at the end of the day
Look across at the machine from the doorway
Check the isolator's label against the isolation list

questions.stem: A contractor's crew arrives to work on a machine you have already isolated. What must happen before they start?
options: They start at once, because you have already locked off
They borrow your lock key to save time during the job
They are briefed, sign on and fit their own locks
They fit only their tags, because the locks are yours

questions.stem: Before the last lock is removed, which check is the isolation supervisor responsible for?
options: That the machine has been cleaned and repainted
That the work is done, guards are on and people are clear
That the operators have all gone on their break
That the spare parts used have been re-ordered

questions.stem: Why are isolations removed in the order the procedure gives when a line is returned to service?
options: So each energy source comes back in a safe order
So the locks go back to the store in number order
So the job finishes before the end of the shift
So operators can start their own machines one by one

questions.stem: An audit of isolations finds a lock with no tag and no entry in the register. What is the right response?
options: Remove the lock at once with bolt cutters and report it later
Stop and trace the owner before anything is changed
Add a tag with your own name on it so it is recorded
Ignore it, because a lock is always better than nothing

questions.stem: Which shutdown task most needs a written risk assessment and method statement?
options: Switching off a desk lamp in an office
Turning off a pedestal fan at its plug
Stopping a hand drill with its trigger
Isolating a press with hydraulics, air and a raised ram

questions.stem: An isolator will not lock in the OFF position. What should you do?
options: Tape the handle in the OFF position and carry on with the job
Take the handle off and keep it in your pocket while you work
Isolate at a lockable point upstream and report the fault
Ask someone to stand next to the isolator for the whole day

questions.stem: Why is it important to know the run-down time of a large fan or flywheel?
options: So that no one opens a guard while it is still turning
So the motor can be restarted before it comes to rest
So the bearings can be greased while it is still running
So the energy can be kept for the next start-up

questions.stem: A lift table must be worked on in the raised position. How is it made safe?
options: Hold it up with the hydraulic pressure and nothing else
Put a wooden crate underneath it as the support
Fit the maker's mechanical stops or rated props
Tie it up with a rope to a beam in the roof

questions.stem: A plastic moulding machine's heaters run very hot. Why is it not enough just to isolate them before work?
options: The parts stay hot for a long time after isolation
The heaters can keep working without any electricity
The heat makes the isolator unsafe to lock off
The heaters will restart if the room gets cold

questions.stem: A pump moves a caustic cleaning chemical. Before the pump is opened, what is needed besides electrical isolation?
options: Only a dust mask and a pair of safety boots
Close, lock and drain the lines; wear the PPE on the SDS
Run the pump dry for a while to empty it first
Spray the pump with water while it is running

questions.stem: Why must machine operators be told before a shutdown, and again before the restart?
options: So that they can sign the maker's warranty card
So that they can leave work early for the day
So that they can switch the machine back on early
So they can plan their work and stay clear at restart

questions.stem: A trainee says 'I know it's off, I saw the light go out', and reaches into the panel. What should you do?
options: Stop them and have them prove dead first
Let them carry on, as the light is a fair sign
Tell them to wear thicker gloves and carry on
Switch the light back on to check the panel

questions.stem: Who switches the supply back on at the end of a group isolation?
options: The first worker to finish their own part of the job
Any operator who needs the machine for production
The contractor whose part of the job took longest
The authorised person, once all locks are off

questions.stem: During isolated work, a worker is hurt and trapped inside a machine. What should happen first?
options: Restore the power at once so the part can be moved off them
Keep the isolation in place and get first aid and help
Remove every lock so that the rescuers can work freely
Ask the injured worker which button should be pressed

questions.stem: After work on a motor, an authorised person runs it for a test. What should the team check during the run?
options: That the machine sounds loud enough to be heard
That the padlocks still fit the isolator hasp
Direction, noise, guards and correct operation
That the operators like the colour of the paint

questions.stem: A damaged isolator was found during the shutdown. What should your report include?
options: Only the name of the operator who was on duty that day
The fault, the risk, the action taken and what is still needed
Just a short note saying 'isolator bad' on the job card
The price of a new isolator and nothing else

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A capacitor of 2 000 µF (0.002 F) is charged to 300 V. Using E = ½CV², how many joules does it hold?
A single-phase supply has a line, a neutral and an earth. How many tests between pairs of conductors are needed to prove it dead?
What do the letters UPS stand for?
What is the name for the time a large fan or flywheel takes to come to rest after it is switched off?
What is the name of the isolation method that uses two closed valves with an open vent valve between them?
On a speed drive, what do the letters STO stand for?
What is the name of the document that lists every energy source and isolation point for one machine, often with photos?
What is the name of the register that shows every isolation now in place on a site?
A speed drive label says to wait 10 minutes after isolation before touching it. You isolated it at 10:52. What is the earliest time you may test its DC bus?
What kind of switch, fitted next to a machine, lets it be isolated and locked off within sight of the worker?
On Jamaica's 110/220 V single-phase supply, what is the voltage between either line and earth, in volts?
What is the name for the formal passing of an isolation from one shift's team to the next?
What is the name of the safety device that stops a machine running when its guard is opened?
What is the name of the rated prop or pin fitted under a raised part of a machine so that it cannot fall?
Which sheet from the chemical's supplier gives its hazards, the PPE to wear and first aid? Give its name or letters.

essays.stem: A new filling machine has been installed in a factory. Explain how you would prepare a machine-specific isolation procedure for it.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start with the maker's manual and the latest electrical, air and hydraulic drawings, then walk round the machine with an operator and a maintenance fitter. I would list every energy source: the main supply, any control or external supplies, a UPS, compressed air, hydraulic pressure, springs, raised parts, hot parts and any chemicals. For each, I would name the isolation point with a unique label, say how it is locked, and say how stored energy is released and checked. I would set the order of shutdown and isolation, the proving-dead points with the tester checked before and after, and the 'try' step. I would add photos of each isolation point and fit matching labels on site. The draft is checked by a second competent person and trialled on the machine, corrected, approved by the supervisor and filed. Staff are trained on it, and it is reviewed whenever the machine is changed.
markingPoints: Uses the manual and latest drawings and surveys with operators and fitters
Lists every energy source, including control supplies and stored energy
Gives each isolation point a unique label, locking method and release method
Sets the order of steps, proving dead and the try step, with photos and labels
Has it checked, trialled, approved, trained and reviewed when the machine changes

essays.stem: You are the isolation supervisor for a weekend shutdown of a bottling line. Electricians, fitters and a contractor will work on it, over two shifts. Describe how you would manage the isolation.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the weekend I would agree the shutdown with production and check the isolation procedures against the drawings. On the day, I would shut down the line in the stated order and carry out the isolations myself or with a second authorised person, locking each point with an isolation lock and tag and proving dead with a tester checked before and after. I would release stored energy and do the try step. The isolation lock keys go into a lockbox. Every worker, including the contractor's crew, is briefed, signs the permit and fits a personal lock to the lockbox, removing it only when they finish. At the change of shift, the new team signs on and fits their locks before the old team removes theirs, and I hand over the permit and register in writing. At the end I check that all work is finished and people are clear before the isolation locks come off.
markingPoints: Plans with production and checks procedures against drawings
Shuts down in order, isolates, locks, tags, proves dead with a checked tester and releases stored energy
Uses a lockbox with every worker's personal lock and a signed permit
Manages the shift handover so locks are never all removed
Checks completion and clearance before removing isolations, keeping records

essays.stem: A machine's speed drive has a DC bus capacitor of 2 200 µF (0.0022 F) which charges to about 300 V in use. Work out the energy stored, explain why it is dangerous, and describe how you make the drive safe before work.
essays.modelAnswer: The energy is E = ½CV² = 0.5 × 0.0022 × 300 × 300 = 0.5 × 0.0022 × 90 000 = 99 J, about 100 J. This is enough to give a severe or fatal shock and to cause burns or a flash if the terminals are shorted. The capacitor keeps this charge after the supply is switched off, so the drive is not safe just because it is isolated. To make it safe, I would stop the motor with its normal control, then isolate the drive's supply at its lockable isolator, lock and tag it, and prove dead at the incoming terminals with a tester checked before and after. I would then wait at least the time on the drive's warning label, and test the DC bus terminals with the approved tester to confirm the voltage has gone. If any voltage remains, I wait longer or discharge it with the maker's method, never with a screwdriver. I would record the checks.
markingPoints: Works out the energy correctly (about 99 J)
Explains the shock, burn and flash danger and that charge stays after isolation
Isolates, locks, tags and proves dead at the incoming terminals with a checked tester
Waits the label time and tests the DC bus before touching
Uses only the maker's discharge method, never a screwdriver, and records the checks

essays.stem: Explain why proving dead on a 220 V supply with two lines, a neutral and an earth needs six tests, and a three-phase supply with a neutral needs ten. Say what you would do if any one test shows a voltage.
essays.modelAnswer: To prove dead, every conductor is tested against every other one, because a voltage could be present between any pair. With L1, L2, neutral and earth there are four conductors, and the pairs are L1–L2, L1–N, L2–N, L1–E, L2–E and N–E, which is six tests. With three lines, a neutral and an earth there are five conductors, and the pairs are L1–L2, L2–L3, L3–L1, each line to neutral (three tests), each line to earth (three tests) and N–E, which is ten. Testing only line to earth could miss a supply from another source, or a voltage on a neutral. The tester is checked on a proving unit before and after. If any test shows a voltage, the circuit is not dead. I would stop, keep everyone clear, recheck that the right isolator is locked, look for a second supply or back-feed, and tell the supervisor. Work starts only after a full set of tests shows dead.
markingPoints: Explains that every pair of conductors must be tested
Lists the six pairs for L1, L2, N and E
Lists the ten pairs for three lines, neutral and earth
Checks the tester before and after
If any voltage is found: stops, rechecks the isolation, looks for other supplies and reports

essays.stem: A water pumping station in rural St. Ann has a mains supply, a standby generator with a changeover switch, and solar panels feeding the pump through a DC isolator and inverter. Describe how you would plan the isolation of the pump motor.
essays.modelAnswer: I would list every source that can feed the pump: the mains, the generator and the solar panels, plus any battery or UPS in the control panel. The plan would isolate each one. The generator is stopped and its auto-start disabled and locked out as the maker says, so it cannot start when the mains goes off. The mains is isolated at a lockable point. The solar DC isolator is opened and locked, and the inverter's AC output isolated. Because the panel cables stay live in daylight up to the DC isolator, I would keep clear of them and mark them. After the isolator locks and tags are on, I would wait the inverter's discharge time and prove dead at the motor and inverter terminals, with the tester checked before and after, and do a try step. I would also isolate and vent the water pressure if the pump is to be opened. All isolations go on the permit and register.
markingPoints: Identifies all sources: mains, generator, solar and any battery or UPS
Stops the generator and disables its auto-start
Isolates the mains, the DC isolator and the inverter output, noting the panel cables stay live in daylight
Waits the inverter discharge time, proves dead with a checked tester and does a try step
Releases water pressure and records the isolations

essays.stem: A personal lock has been left on an isolator, and its owner cannot be found. Explain the procedure for removing it, and why each step matters.
essays.modelAnswer: A personal lock means someone may be working on the machine, so it must never just be cut off. First, the supervisor tries every way to contact the owner by phone and through the team, and checks the sign-in records to see if they have left the site. Second, the machine and the area are searched to make sure no one is inside or near it. Third, a named manager reviews the evidence and authorises the removal in writing, as the procedure says. The lock is then removed by the authorised method, and the event is recorded in the isolation register. The machine stays isolated until a new isolation is in place or it is checked and returned to service. Finally, the owner is spoken to when they return, before they go back to work, so they know their lock was removed and the reason is understood. Each step protects a person who may still be at risk.
markingPoints: Explains that a lock means a person may be at risk and is never just cut off
Tries to contact the owner and checks records
Searches the machine and area
Removal authorised in writing by a named manager and recorded
Speaks to the owner on return; machine stays safe until properly returned to service

essays.stem: After a weekend shutdown in which three trades worked on a production line, describe how you, as supervisor, would return the line to service.
essays.modelAnswer: I would first check with each trade leader that their work is finished and signed off on the permit. I would walk the line to make sure tools, rags and spare parts are removed, guards and covers are refitted and fixed, interlocks are reconnected, and no one is inside any machine. Each worker removes only their own personal lock from the lockbox, and I check the register to see all are off. I would tell production and the operators that the line is about to be restarted and set people clear. Then the isolations are removed in the order the procedure gives, for example air and hydraulics before motion, by the authorised person, who restores the supplies. A test run is done section by section, checking direction, guards, emergency stops and normal running. Any problem stops the run and the line is isolated again. Finally, the permit is closed, the register updated and the line handed back in writing, with any remaining faults reported.
markingPoints: Confirms each trade's work is complete and signed off
Checks tools out, guards and interlocks on and people clear
Each person removes only their own lock; register checked
Informs operators, removes isolations in order and the authorised person restores supplies
Test run with checks, permit closed, records updated and handover in writing

essays.stem: A conveyor started while a fitter's hand was near the belt, but no one was hurt. Explain how you would investigate this near miss and what actions might follow.
essays.modelAnswer: I would make the area safe, isolate the conveyor and stop similar work until we understand what happened. I would speak to the fitter, the operators and anyone involved, separately and without blame, and write down what each saw. I would check the permit, the isolation register and the procedure to see which isolations were made, and compare them with the drawings. Possible causes include locking off the wrong isolator, a second supply such as a control feed or a UPS, a missing try step, someone restarting the conveyor from another station, or an old procedure that did not match the machine. Once the root cause is found, actions might include correcting labels and drawings, updating the procedure, adding a lockable isolator, retraining staff on proving dead and the try step, and auditing other isolations. I would write a report with the findings and actions, share it at a toolbox talk, and check later that the actions were done.
markingPoints: Makes the area safe and stops similar work
Gathers facts from people and records without blame
Checks permit, register, procedure and drawings for the cause
Identifies likely root causes (wrong isolator, second supply, missed try step, outdated procedure)
Sets corrective actions, reports, shares and follows up

essays.stem: Explain the difference between stopping a machine with a control (stop button, emergency stop, guard interlock, PLC or a drive's safe torque off) and isolating it. Why is only isolation used for maintenance?
essays.modelAnswer: A control stop uses the machine's control system to stop the motion. A stop button or a PLC command opens a contactor or tells a drive to stop; an emergency stop and a guard interlock do the same through safety circuits; safe torque off stops the drive giving torque to the motor. In each case the main supply is still connected, so terminals inside the panel, the motor and the drive stay live, and stored energy may remain. A fault, a wiring change, a software error or someone pressing start could make the machine move again. Isolation means disconnecting every live conductor from the supply at an isolating device, with a gap that cannot be closed by a control signal, and locking it off. Then the conductors are proved dead and stored energy released. Only isolation, with locks, tags and proving dead, gives a worker certain protection while their hands are in the machine.
markingPoints: Explains what each control stop does
Explains that the supply stays connected and parts stay live after a control stop
Explains that faults, software or another person can restart the machine
Defines isolation: all live conductors disconnected and locked off
States that isolation with proving dead and releasing stored energy is the only safe basis for maintenance

essays.stem: The main air compressor at a garment factory in Kingston must be shut down for a day of repairs. Explain how you would plan the shutdown with the factory, so that work is safe and production is affected as little as possible.
essays.modelAnswer: I would meet the production manager to agree the best day and time, such as a weekend or a quiet shift, and find out which machines use the compressed air and what will stop. We would plan for the outage: a hired or spare compressor, work moved to machines that do not need air, or staff given other tasks. I would write a schedule with the shutdown time, the isolation, the work steps and the expected restart time, and give it to the people affected, with notices on the machines. I would check the isolation procedure, book the people and parts, and arrange a permit. On the day, the compressor is stopped normally, isolated electrically before the receiver is vented, locked and tagged, proved dead, and the air released and checked at zero. I would keep the factory informed of progress and any delay, and plan the restart and test with production.
markingPoints: Agrees timing with production and identifies affected machines
Plans a way to keep production going (spare compressor or other work)
Writes and shares a schedule and puts up notices
Prepares the isolation procedure, permit, people and parts; isolates before venting
Keeps the factory informed and plans the restart with production

practical1.title: Write and trial a machine isolation procedure, then lead a group isolation with a shift handover
practical1.brief: The assessor provides a training rig: a motor and starter fed from a lockable isolator, a separate lockable control supply, and a small pneumatic cylinder fed through a lockable valve with a vent. The rig is never energised by trainees; only the instructor switches the supply. As a group: (1) survey the rig and its drawings and write a machine-specific isolation procedure listing every energy source, each isolation point with a unique label, how it is locked and how stored energy is released, with a sketch or photo of each point; (2) fit labels to the isolation points that match the procedure; (3) have a second member check the procedure against the rig, then the assessor approves it; (4) the instructor runs the rig; the group stops it with its normal control, and two members carry out the isolations, fit isolation locks and tags, and put the keys in a lockbox; (5) every member fits a personal lock to the lockbox and signs the permit; (6) one member at a time, watched by the assessor, proves dead at the motor terminals and the control circuit (tester checked on a proving unit before and after), the air is vented and the gauge checked, and the try step is done; (7) act out a shift handover: two members leave and two 'new' members sign on and fit their locks first; (8) return to service: tools out, guard on, each member removes their own lock, the register is closed and the instructor restores the supply for the test run. Photograph each stage and hand in the procedure, permit and register.
materials: Training rig with motor, starter, lockable isolator, separate lockable control supply and a pneumatic cylinder with lockable vent valve
Isolation locks, a lockbox, a personal padlock and tag for each member
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit
Labels and a label maker or marker
Isolation procedure template, permit to work and isolation register forms
Basic hand tools for removing and refitting a guard
photos: The written isolation procedure with its sketches or photos
The new labels fitted to each isolation point
Isolators and air valve locked and tagged, with keys in the lockbox
The lockbox with every member's personal lock
The tester on the proving unit, and proving dead at the motor terminals
The air gauge reading zero after venting
The shift handover: new locks on before old locks off
The closed permit and register after return to service
checklist: Identified every energy source on the rig, including the control supply and air
Wrote clear steps with unique labels for each isolation point
Isolated, locked and tagged correctly, with keys in the lockbox
Proved dead between all conductors with the tester checked before and after
Vented the air and confirmed zero pressure; carried out the try step and returned controls to off
Followed the shift handover so the lockbox was never without a lock
Removed only their own lock and checked the area before return to service
Led their stage clearly and kept the records accurate
safety: Only the instructor energises the rig; never work on it live
Keep hands clear of the cylinder until the air is vented and the gauge reads zero
Wear safety glasses when venting air
Stop at once and tell the assessor if any test shows a voltage

practical2.title: Audit the isolations on a training workshop, correct the faults found and report a near miss
practical2.brief: The assessor sets up the Centre's training workshop as a 'site' with several machines or rigs already isolated, and some planted faults, such as a wrong label, a lock with no tag, a register entry that does not match, an isolator that will not lock, a procedure that misses a control supply, and an out-of-date tester check. No machine is energised during the task. The assessor also gives a short written account of a near miss on one machine. As a group: (1) plan the audit and divide the machines between members; (2) check each isolation against its procedure, the register and the drawings, and photograph every finding without removing anyone's lock; (3) agree with the assessor how each fault will be put right, and correct the ones the group may correct: relabel, add a missing tag with the owner's details, isolate upstream at a lockable point where an isolator will not lock, update the procedure, and fix the register; (4) prove dead where a corrected isolation needs it, with the tester checked on a proving unit before and after; (5) investigate the near miss using the documents, and find its likely root cause; (6) write an audit and near-miss report with findings, risks, actions and owners; and (7) give a 10-minute toolbox talk to the assessor on what was found. Each member audits at least one machine, corrects at least one fault and presents part of the talk. Photograph each stage and hand in the report.
materials: Training workshop machines or rigs, isolated by the assessor, with planted faults
Isolation procedures, drawings and the isolation register for each
Spare tags, labels, padlocks and a hasp
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit
Audit checklist, report form and toolbox talk attendance sheet
photos: The audit plan with machines shared out
Proving dead after a corrected isolation, with the tester check
The finished report and the toolbox talk in progress
checklist: Checked isolations against procedures, register and drawings in a planned way
Found the planted faults and recorded each with a photo
Never removed or changed another person's lock
Corrected faults safely, isolating upstream where an isolator would not lock
Proved dead correctly where needed, with the tester checked before and after
Found a likely root cause for the near miss and set sensible actions
Wrote their part of the report clearly and presented part of the toolbox talk
safety: No machine is energised during the task; only the instructor switches supplies
Never remove or cut another person's lock; report it instead
Treat every conductor as live until you have proved it dead yourself
Keep clear of moving or raised parts until they are confirmed safe
